scope: Conventions and measurable starting targets for steering edits. They are engineering heuristics from common synthesis and acoustics practice, not aesthetic verdicts; confirm by rendering and listening.

principles.rule: Amplitude attack shorter than about 2 ms on sustained or low-register sounds produces an audible onset click unless the transient is intended.
principles.check: click_count == 0 on sustained recipes; attack_ms within the recipe range

principles.rule: A release shorter than one period of the lowest note (or under 10 ms) cuts the waveform mid-cycle and clicks at note-off.
Long releases on bass and low pads overlap consecutive notes and smear the low end; bass releases are usually 30-200 ms.
Two oscillators d cents apart beat at f*(2^(d/1200)-1) Hz. About 0.5-8 Hz reads as chorus or movement; above about 15-20 Hz it turns into roughness. The same cents detune beats faster on higher keys.
principles.check: beat rates at the top of the playable range stay below 20 Hz unless roughness is intended

principles.rule: Keep content below about 120 Hz centered and un-detuned: stereo or detuned sub content cancels on mono playback and pumps in level on sustained notes.
Stacked oscillators at octaves (12, 24 semitones) and fifths (7, 19) reinforce the harmonic series; other fixed intervals sound as a chord on every key.
principles.check: coarse offsets in {0, +-7, +-12, +-19, +-24} unless a chord is intended

principles.rule: Coherent oscillators add in amplitude (N*g), uncorrelated detuned voices add in power (sqrt(N)*g). Polyphonic roles need about 8-10 dB headroom per voice so a seven-note chord does not clip.
principles.check: single-voice peak about -12 dBFS or lower for Keys/Pad, about -6 dBFS for mono Bass/Lead

principles.rule: Velocity should change level monotonically. Typical velocity 40->120 level ranges: organ 0-2 dB, pads 4-10 dB, synth bass and leads 4-12 dB, plucks and keys 10-24 dB.
principles.check: rms_dbfs rises with velocity within the recipe velocity_db range

principles.rule: Acoustic and most expressive synth sounds also get brighter with velocity; level-only velocity sounds like a volume knob.
principles.check: centroid_hz at high velocity / low velocity >= 1.05 when a velocity-to-cutoff route exists

principles.rule: Struck and plucked sources decay faster on higher notes (roughly 10-30 % shorter per octave). A constant decay across the keyboard sounds synthetic in the treble and short in the bass.
principles.check: estimated_t60_seconds decreases with pitch on pluck/keys recipes (KeyToDecay < 0)

principles.rule: Perceived loudness should stay roughly even across the playable range; equal-loudness contours make the lowest and highest notes sound quieter at equal RMS.
principles.check: rms spread across test notes within about 6 dB, with no adjacent-zone jump above 3 dB

principles.rule: Adjacent key or velocity zones should be level and tone matched; hard switches without crossfades expose seams.
principles.check: adjacent zone gain difference <= 3 dB; use Low/HighKeyFade or Low/HighVelocityFade for crossfades

principles.rule: Identical retriggers (fixed phase, one sample) sound mechanical on repeated notes. Bass and plucks benefit from phase reset for consistent punch; pads benefit from free-running phase or round-robin variation.
principles.check: repeat the same note 4 times and compare renders with falcon_audio_diff

principles.rule: Build a stable center voice that carries pitch and identity first; add layers only with a stated job (body, air, transient, width).
principles.check: each layer has a role; muting it changes a named feature

sub_bass.name: Sub bass
sub_bass.description: Clean sine/triangle-like low end: stable pitch, mono, short release, modest velocity range.
sub_bass.test_phrase: Repeated 8th notes on E1-C3 at velocities 40/90/120 plus one held 2 s note; check low-end level, release overlap and mono.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Index values are not documented offline; pick the value whose render matches the sine signature.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Bass velocity range 4-12 dB keeps the low end even in a mix.

native_edits.name: PortamentoTime
native_edits.why: Short glide for legato bass lines once a mono/legato PlayMode is selected.

native_edits.name: PlayMode
native_edits.why: Choose the mono/legato mode after reading the live definition; the offline index only gives 0..4.

beyond_builder: Optional gentle saturation (Drive, Tube Amp) adds harmonics so the bass reads on small speakers; re-check stereo and level after inserting.
pitfalls: Detuned or stereo sub content cancels in mono
Release over 200 ms smears repeated notes
Waveform with weak fundamental disappears on small speakers

reese_bass.name: Reese bass
reese_bass.description: Two detuned saws for slow phasing movement over a centered un-detuned sub layer.
reese_bass.test_phrase: Held 2 s notes on E1, C2, G2 and a short riff; confirm slow phasing, solid sub and no level pumping in mono.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Saw layer supplies the harmonics that phase against each other.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Sub layer must be a clean centered fundamental.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Bass velocity range 4-12 dB.

beyond_builder: A low-pass filter (Ladder or Analog Filter) on the saw layer around 300-800 Hz plus a slow LFO on cutoff is the usual Reese motion; a high-pass around 100 Hz on the saw layer keeps the sub clean.
pitfalls: Detuning the sub layer makes the fundamental pump
Too much detune (> 25 cents) reads as out of tune instead of moving

analog_pluck.name: Analog pluck
analog_pluck.description: Fast attack, zero sustain, keytracked decay; level and brightness follow velocity.
analog_pluck.test_phrase: 16th-note arpeggio C3-C6 at mixed velocities plus single notes held past the decay; check decay keytracking and repeated-note consistency.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Bright harmonic-rich source for a pluck.

native_edits.name: KeyToDecay
native_edits.why: Higher notes decay faster, as on plucked strings.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Plucks need a wide velocity response (10-24 dB).

beyond_builder: A filter envelope (Ladder/Analog Filter cutoff modulated by an envelope with about 0.1-0.4 s decay) gives the brightness decay that makes a pluck; target brightness_decay_ratio >= 1.3.
Route velocity to that filter envelope amount so harder notes are brighter.
pitfalls: Constant decay across the keyboard
Level-only velocity response
Attack under 1 ms clicks in the low register

soft_keys.name: Soft synth keys
soft_keys.description: Triangle-like body with a quiet octave partial, piano-like decay to a low sustain.
soft_keys.test_phrase: Four-voice chord progression with sustained chords and a light melody on top; check chord headroom, decay and velocity response.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Mellow odd-harmonic body; the octave partial adds controlled brightness.

native_edits.name: KeyToDecay
native_edits.why: Treble decays faster than bass.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Keys need a wide velocity response.

beyond_builder: A gentle low-pass with velocity-to-cutoff makes soft notes darker; a short tine/contact transient layer can be added at high velocity only.
pitfalls: Chords clip because single-voice level was set by ear on one note
Octave partial too loud reads as organ

warm_pad.name: Warm pad
warm_pad.description: Slow swell, detuned saws for chorus-rate beating, wide but mono-compatible, long release.
warm_pad.test_phrase: Held three- and four-note chords for 4 s with 3 s release; check swell, beating rate, width and mono fold-down.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Rich source; warmth comes from filtering, not from a dull waveform.

native_edits.name: Stereo
native_edits.why: Spread the unison voices for width.

native_edits.name: StereoSpread
native_edits.why: Moderate width keeps mono fold-down acceptable.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Pads need a small velocity range.

beyond_builder: Low-pass around 1.5-4 kHz with a slow LFO (0.1-0.3 Hz) on cutoff gives warmth and movement; chorus or reverb on an aux adds space without moving the center.
pitfalls: Attack under 100 ms turns a pad into keys
Detune fixed in cents beats roughly in the top octave
Width from antiphase content disappears in mono

string_ensemble.name: String ensemble
string_ensemble.description: Three detuned saws, medium bow-like attack, high sustain; vibrato and filtering added after building.
string_ensemble.test_phrase: Slow legato melody and held chords; check attack, ensemble beating and release.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Bowed strings have saw-like spectra.

native_edits.name: VelToAttack
native_edits.why: Harder notes bow in faster.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Moderate velocity range.

beyond_builder: Delayed vibrato: LFO to pitch at 5-6 Hz, 10-25 cents, faded in over 0.3-0.6 s and/or on the mod wheel.
Band-pass/low-pass around 3-5 kHz removes buzz; a formant-like peak near 1-3 kHz adds body.
pitfalls: Static unison without vibrato sounds like an organ
Raw saw buzz above 5 kHz

mono_lead.name: Mono lead
mono_lead.description: Saw plus slightly detuned saw, quick attack, high sustain, short release, glide.
mono_lead.test_phrase: Legato melody with overlapping notes, a few long held notes and repeated staccato notes; check glide, release and sustain stability.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Cutting harmonic-rich lead source.

native_edits.name: PlayMode
native_edits.why: Select the mono/legato mode after reading the live definition.

native_edits.name: PortamentoTime
native_edits.why: 30-100 ms glide for legato phrasing.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Leads need moderate velocity range.

beyond_builder: Vibrato via LFO to pitch at 5-6.5 Hz, 10-30 cents on the mod wheel (target vibrato_depth_cents 10-30 when engaged).
pitfalls: Poly mode loses legato/glide identity
Release over 0.4 s blurs fast phrases
Wide stereo moves the melody off center

brass_synth.name: Synth brass
brass_synth.description: Saws with a swelling attack that speeds up with velocity, mid-high sustain.
brass_synth.test_phrase: Short stabs and held chords at velocities 50/90/127; check attack speed versus velocity and stab release.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Brass spectra are saw-like.

native_edits.name: VelToAttack
native_edits.why: Harder notes speak faster.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Brass needs a pronounced velocity response.

beyond_builder: The defining brass cue is a filter envelope that opens with the attack (about 50-150 ms) and closes to a lower sustain; route velocity to its amount.
pitfalls: Instant attack reads as an organ stab
No velocity-to-attack makes every stab identical

drawbar_organ.name: Drawbar-style organ
drawbar_organ.description: Additive stack at unison, octave and octave-plus-fifth; full sustain, no velocity response.
drawbar_organ.test_phrase: Held chords and a fast run; check constant sustain, quick release and equal level at all velocities.

native_edits.name: Waveform
native_edits.why: Drawbars are sine partials.

native_edits.name: DynamicRange
native_edits.why: Organs do not respond to velocity.

beyond_builder: Rotary or chorus/vibrato effects (Rotary, Rotary Speaker) give the organ motion; key click is a short noise burst, not a 0 ms attack.
pitfalls: Velocity response makes it sound like a synth
0 ms attack/release clicks

moves: Switch toward a saw-like waveform (sine < triangle < square < saw)
Lower cutoff slightly or add a gentle high shelf cut
Add a low-gain octave-down or sub oscillator
Reduce detune/brightness in the upper layers
Add a body layer an octave down
Add a second slightly detuned oscillator
High-pass or low-shelf cut on non-bass layers
Shorten release on bass and low pads
Reduce detune of bright layers in the top octave
Add a quiet high-passed noise layer
Open a high shelf above 10 kHz
Shorter decay to a lower sustain
Add a transient layer at high velocity
Positive VelToAttack inverted for soft notes
Enable oscillator Stereo and raise StereoSpread
Pan layers apart; keep bass/sub centered
Disable Stereo on the core layer
Add a second oscillator 5-15 cents detuned (beating 1-7 Hz at mid keys)
LFO to pitch at 5-6.5 Hz, 10-30 cents, delayed or on the mod wheel
Reduce near-unison detune that causes slow level drift
Release >= max(10 ms, one period of the lowest note)
Add VelToAttack so soft notes swell
more_expressive.cross_render: Compare velocity 40 and 120 renders with falcon_design_verify: velocity level range and brightness ratio should grow
